claims.text: The driver never reached the pickup. The trip record fixes the deadline at 2026-08-17T07:35:00 (scheduled 07:30 plus 5 minutes) and records driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline as false, with arrived_at null; the rider cancelled at 07:37:40, more than two minutes after that deadline. Under POL-NS-24, where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, the rider may cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full. The 5.00 SGD must be returned.

The GPS trace independently corroborates non-arrival rather than contradicting it. The derived arrival check reports corroborated: false and nearest_fix: null, so no fix on this 50-fix, 100%-coverage, 30 s-interval trace falls within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-21 sets for the arrival test; the trace's final fixes from 07:33:10 to 07:37:40 all report speed 0, i.e. the vehicle was stopped and not at the pickup when the rider cancelled. POL-NS-24's arrival deadline is therefore breached on the platform's own telemetry, not merely on the rider's say-so.

The fee has no clause to stand on. POL-NS-22 authorises the 5.00 SGD no-show fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. Here the cancellation was the rider's (cancelled_by RIDER, reason code RIDER_CANCELLED), and no free wait ever began, because under POL-NS-21 the wait for a driver who arrives after the scheduled time runs from arrival, and this record carries no arrival event at all. The condition POL-NS-22 attaches to the charge is absent, so the charge applied at 07:37:44 was not authorised by the no-show policy.

The driver's explanation of 'jam at Sembawang Road' is uncorroborated on this record. The only traffic artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-05055-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0, and under POL-GEN-02 (limb 3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact. POL-NS-24 conditions the refund on arrival by the deadline and provides no traffic defence; no admissible evidence here supplies one, so the delay account cannot displace the deadline breach.

Candour on a point the record does not give the rider: I do not seek the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24, because the driver did attempt contact - an in-app chat message at 07:31:10 and an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation - so the contact obligation in POL-NS-23 is met. But that obligation is a separate test. POL-NS-24 turns solely on arrival by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, and the driver's compliance with POL-NS-23 does not satisfy it or re-authorise the fee.

The rider is presently carrying the charge. The payments ledger shows cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. A FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD - the amount POL-NS-24 directs to be refunded in full - is the ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge, which is what the rider's claim comes down to.

This case should be decided, not escalated. Every fact POL-NS-24 needs - when the driver was due, whether he arrived, and when the rider cancelled - is carried by artifacts the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log), and POL-GEN-02 (limb 2) requires confidence to be held to the weight of those artifacts rather than below it. POL-GEN-26's open-question route is therefore not engaged. At a contested value of 5.00 SGD, with no fraud flag on either profile and no safety indicator, the AI ruling is final under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26.

claims.text: The driver discharged the contact obligation in full. He sent the rider in-app messages at 07:31:10 and 07:36:30 (EV-CHAT-05055) and placed an in-app call at 07:33:20 that the rider answered for 40 seconds (EV-TRIP-05055, in_app_calls, placed_by DRIVER), every one of them before the rider cancelled at 07:37:40; the record's own contact test for this trip returns obligation_met = true. There is therefore no contact-based route to voiding the 5.00 SGD fee, and the rider's filing cannot succeed on the obligation POL-NS-23 imposes.

The fee charged is exactly the fee the policy fixes, and the payment state is the policy-conforming one. The ledger records fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00 with fee_matches_policy = true, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 (EV-FARE-05055, pre-pass status COMPLETE, weight 1.0). POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD, transfers it to the driver as compensation for the time and fuel he spent, and expressly licenses NO_ACTION; NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands (POL-GEN-03), which here leaves the 5.00 SGD charge in the driver's hands and returns nothing to the rider.

The rider gains nothing from the road-conditions point she does not actually plead against a record that has no traffic artifact at all. EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — and a MISSING artifact carries no fact, so it corroborates neither side and cannot be turned against the driver (POL-GEN-02(3), and the weight and disclosure rule in POL-GEN-02(1)-(2)). What the record does carry at full weight is a live trip: 50 fixes at 30 s from 07:13:10 to the 07:37:40 cancellation, 100% coverage, no gap above 120 s, a derived trace distance of 2.448 km at speeds never above 11 km/h, and the vehicle stationary at a single position from 07:33:10 to 07:37:40 (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0). That is a driver held on his approach and in contact with the rider, not a driver who abandoned the booking.

Even if the Tribunal moves the fee, no goodwill credit may be added on top of it. POL-NS-24 makes the 5.00 SGD credit conditional on the driver having ALSO failed to attempt contact; the driver attempted contact three times before the cancellation — two in-app messages and an answered 40-second in-app call (EV-TRIP-05055, EV-CHAT-05055). The structured goodwill_credit_sgd of 5.00 in the ledger's money block (EV-FARE-05055, evidence_id null) is therefore not payable, and the amount at stake is confined to the fee itself.

The fact POL-NS-24 turns on is not established anywhere on this record. trip_record.arrived_at is null (EV-TRIP-05055) and the trace's arrival check returns arrived_at null, nearest_fix null and corroborated false (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0) — no arrival event and no corroborating fix was found; and the one artifact that could show what the road was doing, the traffic advisory, is absent (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). POL-GEN-26 requires that a fact the ruling needs, where the record cannot establish it, go to a human reviewer with the open question stated, and forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of that evidence; POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final only subject to POL-GEN-26. If the Tribunal is not minded to let the fee stand, the conservative course is therefore to hold the 5.00 SGD and escalate, stating the open question: was the driver's non-arrival by 07:35 a no-show, or a congested approach he reported to the rider in real time?

ruling.explanation:
Both parties are told the same thing: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee is refunded in full.

To the rider: your account is borne out. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05055, weight 1.0) fixes the scheduled pickup at 07:30 on 2026-08-17 and the arrival deadline at 07:35 (scheduled plus 5 minutes, POL-NS-24); it records arrived_at null and driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline = false, and the cancellation at 07:37:40 by the rider. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0, 50 fixes, 100% coverage, 30 s interval, no gap over 120 s) corroborates non-arrival rather than contradicting it: no fix falls within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius POL-NS-21 sets, nearest_fix is null and corroborated is false, and the vehicle is stationary at one position from 07:33:10 to 07:37:40 roughly 1.1 km from the pickup. Under POL-NS-24 a driver who has not arrived by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes leaves the rider free to cancel at no charge, and any fee charged is refunded in full. The arrival deadline was breached, so the 5.00 SGD shown in the payments ledger (EV-FARE-05055: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is returned. The charge was in any event not authorised by POL-NS-22, which attaches the fee to the driver cancelling after the free wait; here the rider cancelled, and on this record no free wait ever began because there is no arrival from which it could run (POL-NS-21).

To the driver: your account of the jam and your contact are on the record and I accept them. You messaged the rider at 07:31:10 and 07:36:30 (EV-CHAT-05055) and placed a 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20 that was answered (EV-TRIP-05055, in_app_calls), all before the 07:37:40 cancellation. POL-NS-23's contact obligation is therefore met, and because contact was attempted the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 is not payable. But POL-NS-24 contains no traffic exception: its test is arrival by 07:35, and on a complete, fully-covering trace you had not arrived by then. The driver-side claim that the fee should stand because it matches the policy figure (POL-NS-22) is rejected for that reason; the fee's condition was not met.

The request to escalate under POL-GEN-26 is rejected. The fact POL-NS-24 turns on — whether the driver arrived by the deadline — is established, in the negative, by two complete weight-1.0 artifacts; it is not a fact the record cannot carry. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact for either side, so nothing corroborates or refutes the jam; it simply does not help the driver displace the deadline.

No referral is produced. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so no POL-NS-22 amount referral arises; the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is not payable; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag is not engaged because that counter is absent from the rider profile and the fee does not stand. At a contested value of 5.00 SGD, with no fraud flag and no safety indicator, POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make this ruling final. Confidence is 0.9, within the 1.0 cap set by the weight-1.0 trip record and GPS trace that carry the deciding fact.

ruling.explanation:
The 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-05055 is refunded to the rider in full.

Why. The scheduled pickup was 07:30 on 17 Aug 2026. POL-NS-24 (Driver no-show) says that if the driver has not arrived by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes — here 07:35:00 — the rider may cancel at no charge, and any fee charged is refunded in full. The trip record shows no arrival: arrived_at is empty and the record's own deadline check returns arrived_by_deadline false against the 07:35:00 deadline (EV-TRIP-05055, weight 1.0). The GPS trace confirms it independently: 50 fixes at 30-second intervals from 07:13:10 to the moment of cancellation at 07:37:40, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s, and from 07:33:10 to 07:37:40 the vehicle is stationary roughly 1.1 km from the pickup, with no fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0). The rider cancelled at 07:37:40, more than two minutes past the 07:35 deadline, and the payments ledger shows the 5.00 SGD fee charged (cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, EV-FARE-05055, weight 1.0). The payment recorded by the ledger is therefore returned.

To the driver. You met the contact obligation: an in-app message at 07:31:10, an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20, a second message at 07:36:30, all before the 07:37:40 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05055, EV-TRIP-05055, weight 1.0). So the fee is not voided for want of contact under POL-NS-23, and your request that no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit be added is accepted — POL-NS-24 makes that credit conditional on a failure to attempt contact, which did not happen, so no credit is added on top of the refund. But the contact rule and the arrival rule are separate tests, and it is the arrival test that decides this case. POL-NS-22 authorises the fee only when the driver cancels after the free wait; here the rider cancelled, and the free wait never began, because under POL-NS-21 it runs from the driver's arrival and there was no arrival. The fee matching the 5.00 SGD policy figure does not make the charge lawful.

On the jam account. The rider's point that the delay explanation is uncorroborated was not admitted through the pre-pass because it cited the absent traffic advisory without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue; the missing advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, weight 0.0) carries no fact for either side and corroborates neither. Your messages and your counterparty statement are noted as evidence of what was happening, but POL-NS-24 gives no traffic exception to the 07:35 deadline, and no admissible artifact establishes road conditions. The escalation route in POL-GEN-26 is not engaged: the fact the rule turns on — whether the driver arrived by 07:35 — is established by the record, not unavailable.

Finality. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's first band (10.00 SGD), neither profile carries a fraud flag, and no safety indicator is present, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 this ruling is final.

ruling.explanation:
Rider, your 5.00 SGD cancellation fee is refunded in full. Driver, no compensation is payable.

What decides it — POL-NS-24 (driver no-show). Your pickup was scheduled for 07:30 (EV-TRIP-05055), so under POL-NS-24 the driver had to be at the pickup by 07:35, the scheduled time plus the 5-minute free wait. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05055, weight 1.0) records arrived_at null and driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline false. The driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0; 50 fixes at 30 s, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s) carries the arrival test's own result — corroborated false, nearest_fix null, no fix within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — and its last fixes, from 07:33:10 to the 07:37:40 cancellation, show the vehicle stationary about 1.1 km short of the pickup. You cancelled at 07:37:40, more than two minutes past the deadline. On those two COMPLETE artifacts the driver failed to arrive by the deadline: the fee is voided and the whole 5.00 SGD (fee_charged_sgd 5.00; total_charged 5.00; refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is returned. That is FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03.

The driver's request to escalate under POL-GEN-26 is not accepted. POL-GEN-26 applies where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired. The arrival fact is established, not missing: the trip record and the GPS trace that the arrival test reads are both COMPLETE at weight 1.0, the test ran, and it found no arrival. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3), and POL-NS-24 gives no traffic defence in any event. The driver's statement that he was held in a jam is not a clause of the no-show policy and does not displace the deadline.

The contact points are accepted on both sides and do not change the outcome. The driver did discharge the POL-NS-23 contact obligation — an in-app message at 07:31:10, a second at 07:36:30, and an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20 (EV-CHAT-05055, EV-TRIP-05055), all before the 07:37:40 cancellation — so POL-NS-23 does not void the fee. That is a separate test from POL-NS-24, and passing it does not cure the failure to arrive by the deadline; the driver's NO_ACTION argument therefore does not stand. Because contact was attempted, the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that POL-NS-24 conditions on a failure to attempt contact is not payable, and no referral is added for it.

The rider's further point that the charge lacked a clause to stand on is consistent with this result, but the refund rests on POL-NS-24.

No referral is produced. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises; rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, which POL-NS-25 requires, is not present in the profile (and the fee does not stand); and no safety flag or fraud flag arises (POL-GEN-21, POL-GEN-22).

Confidence: the deciding fact is carried by the trip record and the GPS trace, each at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. At a contested value of 5.00 SGD with no fraud flag on either profile, POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 make the AI ruling final at any confidence; confidence is 0.95.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver — this is decided on the platform's own records.

Outcome: the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee is refunded in full (FULL_REFUND). The rider gets back the 5.00 SGD shown as 'cancellation_fee' and 'total_charged' on the payments ledger (EV-FARE-05055). No compensation is payable to the driver.

Why. POL-NS-24 gives the rider a no-charge cancellation where the driver does not arrive at the pickup by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes. The scheduled pickup was 07:30 (EV-TRIP-05055), so the deadline was 07:35. The trip record carries no arrival event at all — arrived_at is null and arrived_by_deadline is false. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05055, complete, 50 fixes at 30-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 seconds) independently confirms it: no fix comes within the 50 m arrival radius POL-NS-21 sets for this STANDARD pickup, and the last fixes, from 07:33:10 through the 07:37:40 cancellation, are stationary roughly 1.1 km short of the pickup. The driver therefore did not arrive by 07:35, and the rider's cancellation at 07:37:40 was the cancellation POL-NS-24 permits. The rider's submission that the 5.00 SGD should be returned is accepted.

The driver's points. I accept that the driver met the contact obligation in POL-NS-23: he sent in-app messages at 07:31:10 and 07:36:30 and placed an answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20, all before the cancellation (EV-CHAT-05055, EV-TRIP-05055). That means the fee is not voided on contact grounds, and it also means no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due under POL-NS-24, because that credit needs a failure to attempt contact as well — both sides are right on that point, and no referral arises. But the contact obligation is a separate test; it does not satisfy POL-NS-24's arrival deadline and does not re-authorise the charge. Nor does POL-NS-22 save the fee: it authorises the 5.00 SGD only when the driver cancels after the free wait, whereas here the rider cancelled and no free wait ever began, because under POL-NS-21 the wait for a driver who has not arrived does not run. The ledger figure of 5.00 SGD 'fee_charged_sgd' matching the 5.00 SGD 'policy_fee_sgd' shows only the amount was right, not that the charge was authorised.

The escalation request under POL-GEN-26 is refused. The facts POL-NS-24 needs — the deadline, whether the driver arrived, and when the rider cancelled — are carried by artifacts the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the record affirmatively shows non-arrival rather than leaving it unestablished. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05055-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; a missing artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)), it is not needed for the no-show test, and it opens no question. The driver's 'jam' account, in his statement and chat messages, explains the delay but POL-NS-24 attaches no traffic defence to the arrival deadline.

At a contested value of 5.00 SGD, with no fraud flag on either profile and no safety indicator, the AI ruling is final (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26). Because every artifact carrying the deciding fact is at weight 1.0, confidence is not depressed by impairment (POL-GEN-02(2)); I set it at 0.9.

But that obligation is a separate test. POL-NS-24 turns solely on arrival by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, and the driver's compliance with POL-NS-23 does not satisfy it or re-authorise the fee.

The rider is presently carrying the charge. The payments ledger shows cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. A FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD - the amount POL-NS-24 directs to be refunded in full - is the ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge, which is what the rider's claim comes down to.

This case should be decided, not escalated. Every fact POL-NS-24 needs - when the driver was due, whether he arrived, and when the rider cancelled - is carried by artifacts the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log), and POL-GEN-02 (limb 2) requires confidence to be held to the weight of those artifacts rather than below it. POL-GEN-26's open-question route is therefore not engaged. At a contested value of 5.00 SGD, with no fraud flag on either profile and no safety indicator, the AI ruling is final under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26.

The driver discharged the contact obligation in full. He sent the rider in-app messages at 07:31:10 and 07:36:30 (EV-CHAT-05055) and placed an in-app call at 07:33:20 that the rider answered for 40 seconds (EV-TRIP-05055, in_app_calls, placed_by DRIVER), every one of them before the rider cancelled at 07:37:40; the record's own contact test for this trip returns obligation_met = true. There is therefore no contact-based route to voiding the 5.00 SGD fee, and the rider's filing cannot succeed on the obligation POL-NS-23 imposes.

The fee charged is exactly the fee the policy fixes, and the payment state is the policy-conforming one. The ledger records fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00 with fee_matches_policy = true, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 (EV-FARE-05055, pre-pass status COMPLETE, weight 1.0). POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD, transfers it to the driver as compensation for the time and fuel he spent, and expressly licenses NO_ACTION; NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands (POL-GEN-03), which here leaves the 5.00 SGD charge in the driver's hands and returns nothing to the rider.

The rider gains nothing from the road-conditions point she does not actually plead against a record that has no traffic artifact at all. EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — and a MISSING artifact carries no fact, so it corroborates neither side and cannot be turned against the driver (POL-GEN-02(3), and the weight and disclosure rule in POL-GEN-02(1)-(2)). What the record does carry at full weight is a live trip: 50 fixes at 30 s from 07:13:10 to the 07:37:40 cancellation, 100% coverage, no gap above 120 s, a derived trace distance of 2.448 km at speeds never above 11 km/h, and the vehicle stationary at a single position from 07:33:10 to 07:37:40 (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0). That is a driver held on his approach and in contact with the rider, not a driver who abandoned the booking.

Even if the Tribunal moves the fee, no goodwill credit may be added on top of it. POL-NS-24 makes the 5.00 SGD credit conditional on the driver having ALSO failed to attempt contact; the driver attempted contact three times before the cancellation — two in-app messages and an answered 40-second in-app call (EV-TRIP-05055, EV-CHAT-05055). The structured goodwill_credit_sgd of 5.00 in the ledger's money block (EV-FARE-05055, evidence_id null) is therefore not payable, and the amount at stake is confined to the fee itself.

The fact POL-NS-24 turns on is not established anywhere on this record. trip_record.arrived_at is null (EV-TRIP-05055) and the trace's arrival check returns arrived_at null, nearest_fix null and corroborated false (EV-GPS-05055, weight 1.0) — no arrival event and no corroborating fix was found; and the one artifact that could show what the road was doing, the traffic advisory, is absent (EV-ADVIS-05055-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). POL-GEN-26 requires that a fact the ruling needs, where the record cannot establish it, go to a human reviewer with the open question stated, and forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of that evidence; POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final only subject to POL-GEN-26. If the Tribunal is not minded to let the fee stand, the conservative course is therefore to hold the 5.00 SGD and escalate, stating the open question: was the driver's non-arrival by 07:35 a no-show, or a congested approach he reported to the rider in real time?
